scenes.question:
Build a complete, beautiful three.js kinetic sculpture for a developer livestream.
Return ONLY a complete HTML document, no Markdown fences and no explanation.
Use THREE from the provided classic script ./vendor/three.min.js (three.js 0.160.1).
No other imports, dependencies, network calls, external assets, logos, people, or eval.

The artwork: a small luminous cobalt core with three orbiting, tilted metallic rings,
warm copper accents, and hundreds of tiny particles that travel in coherent orbital
paths. It should feel like a physical museum sculpture, not a random particle cloud.
Create depth through geometry, perspective, materials, and lighting. Use a dark navy
background. Fill the available 16:9 viewport with a legible, balanced composition.
Avoid huge white lighting hotspots. Use simple procedural geometry and bounded GPU work.

Include working native Pause/Resume and Reset view buttons, a speed range slider,
mouse or pointer drag to orbit the view, responsive resize, and a clear title.
Respect prefers-reduced-motion by starting paused. Show an explicit readable error
if WebGL is unavailable. Keep all text at least 16px, with strong contrast and visible
keyboard focus. Use requestAnimationFrame, cap pixel ratio at 2, and no shadows or
postprocessing. Make it run offline when served alongside the provided three.js file.
Don't assume OrbitControls or any add-ons are available. Include all implementation
inside this single document. Aim for a polished scene, not a technical wireframe.
Keep the implementation concise: at most 250 lines and 18,000 characters of HTML.

caveats: Three generated scenes use the identical prompt and a 12,000 completion-token cap. One sample per setting, not a benchmark or causal quality ranking.
reasoning_effort none, low, and high were accepted by the live API. Reasoning tokens are included in output_tokens, not additional tokens.
The service reports model Kimi-K3.1; management-plane deployment is MoonshotAI Kimi-K3.1-Pro version 2026-11-04. Do not hide this naming difference.
Some real calls returned an endpoint-not-found error; an early scene hit its token cap and another lacked a complete HTML document. Live runner has no retries or recorded fallback.
Current Nov 9 catalog labels GA; the supplied weekly draft said preview. No historical catalog snapshot establishes the lifecycle label by Nov 6 12:01 PST.
Catalog lists 1,048,576 context tokens; Learn describes 1,000,000 input tokens and 262,144 output tokens. Use 'roughly one million' in narration.
Long-context check is a bounded public changelog corpus, not a million-token capacity or attention benchmark.
Generated scene code is unedited and runs inside an opaque-origin, allow-scripts-only iframe with network, forms, and navigation blocked by CSP/sandbox.
The three.js runtime is pinned and vendored with its MIT license. Recorded scenes require WebGL but no model access or network dependency.
USD announcement prices are $2.30 input, $0.23 cached input, $11.50 output per million tokens. Actual agreement pricing can differ.
